string.name: learn011
string.Data:
Introduction

&emsp Java is a high-level object oriented programing language, created by a team led by James Gosling for Sun Microsystems in the early 90\' but now is owned by Oracle.

&emsp High-level means that it use natural language elements which are easier to be understood by humans.

&emsp Object oriented means that is based on the concept of \"objects\".

string.name: learn021
string.Data:
Compilers

&emsp In order to run a Java program you need to download the JDK (Java Development Kit) from \'www.oracle.com\' and a compiler.

&emsp After downloading and installing the JDK, go in the installation folder and copy the path, it should look something like \'C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-9.0.4\\bin\'.

&emsp Then add the path to the \'System variables\' in \'Environment variables\' from the \'Advanced\' section of \'System Properties\'.

resources.string:
&emsp If the path of the JDK is set, the next step is to download and install a compiler.

&emsp A Java compiler is a program that takes the text file work of a developer and compiles it into a platform-independent Java file.

&emsp Java compilers include the Java Programming Language Compiler (javac), the GNU Compiler for Java (GCJ), the Eclipse Compiler for Java (ECJ) and Jikes.

string.name: learn031
string.Data:
First program

&emsp After installing the JDK and a compiler we are ready to write the first program.

&emsp First we need to open the compiler and create a new project and a new class or just open the Notepad/Notepad++ and write the code below. The name file must be saved with the class method and with the extension java like \'FirstClass.java\'.

string.name: learn032
string.Data:
&emsp Every java program must have:
1. a class:
&emsp -is the first thing you will write when you create a java program
&emsp -the name of that class is usually capitalized
2. a main method:
&emsp -a method is like a list of things that the compiler need to do
&emsp -whenever a java program is running, the computer look for the main method

string.name: learn033
string.Data:
&emsp After you wrote the code, run the program in your compiler.

&emsp If you wrote it in Notepad, open the \'Command Prompt\' in the folder you saved the file and write the command \'javac FirstClass.java\'.

&emsp This will compile your program and create a file named FirstClass.class.

&emsp In order to run it we need to add another line with the command \'java FirstClass\'.

&emsp This should be the result:

resources.string: Which is the command you need to compile a java file?

string.Data:
Comments

&emsp Comments are lines of code that are not being compiled.
&emsp They are included in the code by the programmers to explain what the code is doing.

Java has 3 types of comments:
1. single-line
2. multi-line
3. documentation comments

string.name: learn051
string.Data:
Variables

A variable is a container that holds values.

A java variable has:
&emsp 1. a data type
&emsp 2. a name
&emsp 3. a value

&emsp Syntax:
dataType variableName = value;

string.name: learn052
string.Data:
Data type:

&emsp -if it is a whole number such -110 or 80 it will be an int (integer)
&emsp -if it is a floating-point or real number such as -5.67 or 32.5623 it will be a float or a double
&emsp -if it is a text such as \"Hello World\" it will be a String
&emsp -and if it is a variable that signifies true or false than it will be a boolean

Name:

&emsp -the name should start with a letter and may contain a number or an underline

Value:

&emsp -the value must match the data type

resources.string: What is a variable made of?

string.Data:

float floatVariable = 10f ;
double doubleVariable = 10.0 ;

String stringVariable = \"10\" ;
boolean booleanVariable = true ;

string.name: learn061
string.Data:
Operators

&emsp Java provides a rich set of operators to manipulate variables.

&emsp The most used operators are:
-arithmetic operators
-relational operators
-logical operators
-assignment operators
-bitwise operators
-misc operators
&emsp For now we will only talk about arithmetic and assignment operators.

string.name: learn062
string.Data:
&emsp

Arithmetic operators:


&emsp - arithmetic operators are used in mathematical expressions in the same way that they are used in algebra.

&emsp Example: +(Addition), -(Subtraction), *(Multiplication), /(Division), %(Modulus), ++(Increment), --(Decrement)

string.name: learn063
string.Data:
Assignment operators:


&emsp - assignment operators are similar with arithmetic operators but besides the calculations (where is the case) the result is already assigned to the variable.

&emsp Example: =(Assignment), +(Addition and assignment), -(Subtraction and assignment), *(Multiplication and assignment), /(Division and assignment), %(Modulus and assignment)
&emsp We will talk about the others operators in the next lessons.

resources.string: When should be used an assignment operator?

&emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp // subfix => result = a++ = 10
&emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp // (+1 after the assignment of result)
&emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp // => (and than) a++ = a+1 => 11
a=10

&emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp // prefix => --a = a-1 = 10-1 = 9
&emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp &emsp // => result = --a = 9
a=10

string.name: learn121
string.Data:
If statement

&emsp The if statements are used for conditional statements.
&emsp A conditional statement is used to perform different action based on different conditions.
&emsp If statements are used when you have a condition and if that condition is accomplished the instruction is executed.
&emsp There can be as many if conditions as you need.

&emsp Syntax:
if(condition){
&emsp &emsp//then instruction
}

string.name: learn122
string.Data:
&emsp Example: If a is grater than 10, then write \'a\' is grater then 10\'.
-\'if\' is the keyword
-\'a is grater than 10\' is the condition
-\'then write \"a is grater than 10\" \' is the instruction

&emsp There are two possibilities:
1. a will be grater than 10
2. a will be less than 10

resources.string: What will happen if the \'if\' condition is true?
the program will not enter the if statement
the instruction will be partially executed

string.name: codelearn122
string.Data:
if(a>10){ // condition
&emsp &emsp // instructions
&emsp &emsp System.out.println( \"a is grater than 10\");
}

// &emsp Possibility 1 (int a=11):
// a=11 => a greater than 10 => condition is true
// => the program will enter into the if statement
// => the instruction will be executed
// => the output will be "a is grater than 10"

// &emsp Possibility 2 (int a=9):
// a=9 => a not greater than 10 => condition is false
// => the program will not enter into the if statement
// => the instruction will not be executed

string.name: learn131
string.Data:
Else statement

&emsp Else statements are used when you have a condition and if that condition is not accomplished the else instruction is executed.
&emsp There can be just one else statement attached to the same if statement.

&emsp Syntax:
if(condition){
&emsp &emsp//if instruction
}
else{
&emsp &emsp//else instructions
}

string.name: learn132
string.Data:
&emsp Example: If a is greater than 10, write \'a is greater then 10\', else write \'a is less then 10\'.
-\'if\' and \'else\' are the keywords
-\'a is greater than 10\' is the condition
-\'then write \"a is greater than 10\" \' is the instruction from if
-\'write \"a is not greater then 10\"\' is the instruction from else

&emsp There are two possibilities:
1. a will be grater than 10
2. a will be less than 10

resources.string: In an \'if/else\' condition. What will happen if the \'if\' condition is false?
the else instruction will be executed
the if instruction will be executed
the else instruction will be executed

string.Data:
if(a>1){ // condition

// &emsp Possibility 2 (int a=9):

string.name: learn141
string.Data:
Else if statement

&emsp Else if statements are used when you have a condition and if the first condition is not accomplished, the else if condition is verified, and if true the \'elseif\' instruction is executed.
&emsp After else if statements can be also an else statement.
&emsp There can be as many else if condition attach to the if statement as you need.

&emsp Syntax:
if(condition){
&emsp &emsp //if instruction
}
else if(other condition){
&emsp &emsp //else if instruction
}
else{
&emsp &emsp //else instructions
}

string.name: learn142
string.Data:
&emsp Example: If a is grater than 10, write \'a is grater then 10\', else if a is equal to 10 write \'a is equal then 10\', else write \'a is less to 10\'.
-\'if\', \'else if\' and \'else\' are the keywords
-\'a is grater than 10\' is the condition from if
-\'a is equal to 10\' is the condition from else if
-\'then write \"a is grater then 10\" \' is the instruction from if
-\'then write \"a is equal then 10\" \' is the instruction from else if
-\'write \"a is less than 10\"\' is the instruction from else

&emsp There are three possibilities:
1. a will be grater than 10
2. a will be equal to 10
3. a will be less than 10

resources.string: How many times you can use an \'else if\' statement after an if?
as many time as it needed
as many time as it needed

string.name: codelearn142
string.Data:
if(a>1){ // condition
&emsp &emsp // if instructions
&emsp &emsp System.out.println( \"a is grater than 10\");
}
else if(a==10){ // condition
&emsp &emsp // else if instructions
&emsp &emsp System.out.println( \"a is equal to 10\");
}
else{
&emsp &emsp // else instructions
&emsp &emsp System.out.println( \"a is less than 10\");
}

// &emsp Possibility 1 (int a=11):
// a=11 => a greater than 10 => if condition is true
// => the program will enter into the if statement
// => the \'if\' instruction will be executed
// => the output will be \"a is grater than 10\"

// &emsp Possibility 2 (int a=10):
// a=10 => a not greater than 10
// => if condition is false
// => a equal to 10 => else if condition is true
// => the program will enter into the else if statement
// => the \'else if\' instruction will be executed
// => the output will be \"a is equal to 10\"

// &emsp Possibility 3 (int a=9):
// a=9 => a not greater or equal to 10
// => if and else if conditions are false
// => the program will enter into the else statement
// => the \'else\' instruction will be executed
// => the output will be \"a is less than 10\"

string.name: learn151
string.Data:
Other java operators

Relational operators:


&emsp - relational operators are used in conditions to compare some values.

&emsp Example: ==(Equal to), !=(Not equal to), >(Greater than), <(Less than), >=(Greater than or equal to), <=(Less than or equal to)

string.name: learn152

Logical operators


- logical operators are used when making multiple comparisons in a condition.
Example: &&(Logical and), ||(Logical or), !(Logical not)

string.name: learn161
string.Data:
Switch statement

&emsp Besides if, switch statement is also used in conditional statements.
&emsp Unlike the condition from if statement, switch is coordinated by a variable, expression.
&emsp Depending on the variable value, it will enter on a case.

Syntax:
switch(expression){
&emsp case value:
&emsp &emsp &emsp // instruction
&emsp &emsp &emsp break; // optional
&emsp case otherValue:
&emsp &emsp &emsp // other instruction
&emsp &emsp &emsp break; // optional
&emsp default: // optional
&emsp &emsp &emsp // default instruction
}

string.name: learn162
string.Data:
&emsp Example: If a=1, then write \'a=1\', if a=2, then write \'a=2\', if a=3, then write \'a=3\'.
- \'switch\' and \'case\' are keywords
- \'a\' is the variable
- \'1\', \'2\' and \'3\' are possible values
- if the variable is equal to one of the values, it will execute the instruction.

&emsp After it enters in one of the cases, the instruction will run until the switch is over or it meets the \'break\' keyword.
&emsp If the value of the variable is not in one of the cases than he will go on default case.
- \'switch\', \'case\', \'break\' and \'default\' are keywords
- \'a\' is the variable
- \'1\', \'2\' and \'3\' are possible values
- if the variable is equal to one of the values, it will execute the instruction of that case until meets break or the switch is over

&emsp There are four possibilities:
1. a is equal to 1
2. a is equal to 2
3. a is equal to 3
4. a is none of the above

string.name: codelearn162
string.Data:
switch(a){
&emsp // expression
&emsp case 1:// value of case 1
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println( \"case 1\"); break;
&emsp case 2:// value of case 2
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println( \"case 2\"); break;
&emsp case 2:// value of case 3
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println( \"case 3\"); break;
&emsp default:// default value
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println( \"default\");
}

// &emsp Possibility 1 (int a=1):
// the value of a is 1
// => the correct case will be case 1
// => the output will be \"case 1\"

// &emsp Possibility 2 (int a=2):
// the value of a is 2
// => the correct case will be case 2
// => the output will be \"case 2\"

// &emsp Possibility 3 (int a=3):
// the value of a is 3
// => the correct case will be case 3
// => the output will be \"case 3\"

// &emsp Possibility 4 (int a=4):
// the value of a is 4
// => there is no case with value 4
// => the correct case will be default
// => the output will be \"default\"

string.name: learn211
string.Data:
While loop

&emsp While is a loop that execute the block of instruction code as long as the condition is true.
&emsp While loop can run infinitely if the condition is always true.

&emsp Syntax:
while(condition){
&emsp //instructions
}

string.name: learn212
string.Data:
&emsp Example: While a is greater than 0, write \'a\' and make a=a+1.
- \'while\' is a keyword
- \'a is greater than 0\' is the condition
- \' write \"a\" and make a=a+1\' are the instructions

&emsp There are two possibilities:
1. a is grater than 0
2. a is less or equal to 0

resources.string: How many times will run a while loop, if the condition is always \'true\'?

string.name: codelearn212
string.Data:
while(a>0){ // condition
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println(a);
&emsp a--;
}

// &emsp Possibility 1 (int a=2):
// a is equal to 2 => a greater than 0
// => the program will enter into the while
// => execute instruction => the output will be \"2\"
// => a-- => a=2-1 => a=1
// a is equal to 1 => a greater than 0
// => the program will continue the while
// => execute instruction => the output will be \"1\"
// => a-- => a=1-1 => a=0
// a is equal to 0 => a is not greater than 0
// => the program will exit from the while

// &emsp Possibility 2 (int a=-1):
// a is equal to -1 => a is not greater than 0
// => the program will exit from the while

string.name: learn221
string.Data:
Do while loops

The difference between while and do while is that in the second one, the block of code will run at least once.

&emsp Syntax:
do{
&emsp //instructions
}while(condition);

string.name: learn222
string.Data:
&emsp Example: Write \'a\' and make a=a+1, while a is greater than 0.
- \'do\' \'while\' is a keyword
- \'a is greater than 0\' is the condition
- \' write \"a\" and make a=a+1\' are the instructions

&emsp There is just one possibility:
1. a is greater, equal or less

do while runs at least once
do while runs at least once

string.name: codelearn222
string.Data:
do{
&emsp // instructions
&emsp System.out.println(a);
&emsp a--;
}
while(a>0); // condition

// &emsp Possibility 1 (int a=0):
// any value would have \'a\'
// => the program will enter into the do while
// => execute instruction => the output will be \"0\"
// => a-- => a=0-1 => a=-1
// a is equal to -1 => a is not greater than 0
// => the program will exit from the while

string.name: learn231
string.Data:
Arrays

&emsp An array is a collection of variables of the same type.
It is useful when you have many variables as numbers and you want to store them in order to be easy to use.

&emsp Syntax:
-there are two types of declaring an array:
&emsp -> dataType[] arrayName = new dataType[size];
&emsp -> dataType[] arrayName = {values with commas};

string.name: learn232
string.Data:
&emsp Example:
Suppose you need three numbers 1,2,3.
Instead of declaring three variables \'int a=1, b=2, c=3;\' you can use an array with size 3 \'int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3};\'.

string.name: learn233
string.Data:
&emsp Example:
1. We have an array of two integers \'int[] numbers = {5,10}\' and we want to display their values \' System.out.println("numbers[0]= " + numbers[0] + ", numbers[1]="+ numbers[1])\'.
2. We have an array of two integers \'int[] numbers = new int[2]\' and we want to give them some values \' numbers[0]=5, numbers[1]=10\'.
In this example \'0\' and \'1\' are the index of the array, an array count starts from 0 NOT from 1.

resources.string: What is the correct declaration of an array of 2 integers?

string.name: codelearn232
string.Data:
// Variables:
int a=1, b=2, c=3;

// Array:
int[] numbers={1,2,3};

numbers[0]=5;

string.name: learn241
string.Data:
For loop

&emsp For is a loop that execute the block of instructions code as long as the condition is true.

&emsp Syntax:
for(initialization; termination/condition; increment;){
&emsp //instructions
}

string.name: learn242
string.Data:
&emsp Example: For i equals 0, to 2, from 1 to 1, write \'i\'.
- \'for\' is a keyword
- \'i equals 0\' is the initialization
- \'to 2\' is the termination
- \'from 1 to 1\' is the increment
- \'write \'i\' is the instruction

string.name: learn243
string.Data:
Initialization, termination and increment are optional if they are done somewhere in the code.
If the termination is not written and is no code which make possible exit from the \'for\' the for will run infinite.

resources.string: What will happen, if \'for\' loop has no termination and no alternative for it?
for runs for an infinite time
for runs for an infinite time

string.name: codelearn242
string.Data:
for(int i=0;i<2; i++){
&emsp System.out.println(i);
}

// Explanation:
// 1. initialization: int i=0;
// 2. termination(condition): i<2; => true
// 3. instruction: System.out.println(a);
// => output:0
// 4. increment: i++; => i=1
// 5. = 2. termination(condition): i<2; => true
// 6. = 3. instruction: System.out.println(a);
// => output:1
// 7. = 4. increment: i++; => i=2
// 8. = 2. termination(condition): i<2; => false
// 9. exit \'for\'

string.name: codelearn243
string.Data:
// alternative for initialization:
int i=0;

for(;;){

&emsp // alternative for termination:
&emsp if(i<2){
&emsp &emsp break;
&emsp }

&emsp System.out.println(i);

&emsp // alternative for increment:
&emsp i++;
}

string.name: learn251
string.Data:
For and arrays

&emsp Most of the time for loop is used when working with arrays.

&emsp Example 1:
When we want to initialize all the elements of an array the easiest way to do this is with a for.

string.name: learn252
string.Data:
&emsp Example 2:
When we want to display all the elements of an array.

string.name: codelearn251
string.Data:

}

// array[0]=0;
// array[1]=1;
// array[2]=2;
// array[3]=3;
// array[4]=4;

string.Data:

for(int i=0;i<3; i++){
System.out.println(array[i]);

string.name: learn261
string.Data:
For each loop

&emsp For each it is similar to \'for\' loop, but it has no termination or iteration, only the initialization and the array or collection which he will go through.

&emsp Syntax:
for(initialization : array/collection){
&emsp //instructions
}

string.name: learn262
string.Data: &emsp Example: For each element from array write the value of the element.

resources.string: What is the correct syntax for going through and display an integer array with \'for each\' loop?

string.name: codelearn262
string.Data:
int array={0,1,2};
for(int i:array){
&emsp System.out.println(i);
}

// output:
// 0
// 1
// 2

string.name: learn311

Object-Orientated Programing

Methods

&emsp A Method is a class function, in real-word methods are similar to behavior of a class.

&emsp Syntax:
dataType methodName(parameters){
&emsp // Instructions
}

&emsp A method, unlike attributes, can have the data type \'void\' with means that it will not return some value.
In methods all the others data types return a value.
The \'parameters\' are optional and represent some variables, which were declared outside the method, and which will be used in that method.

string.name: learn421
string.Data:
Access modifiers and Encapsulation

Access modifiers

&emsp Access modifiers are use to set access level for classes, attributes, methods and constructors.
There are 4 access modifiers:
&emsp -> private: the information is visible only in that class
&emsp -> public: the information is visible in every other class
&emsp -> protected: the information is visible to the subclasses of the class (inheritance)
&emsp -> no keyword, which means is the default and will be visible to the package
&emsp The access modifiers are written in the declarations before the data types.

&emsp Example:
We have the Apple class.
With attributes: public color, private dimension, protected type and default bought.
For the Program class which is in the same package with Apple class, we will only access the information with public and with no keyword.

string.name: learn422
string.Data:
Encapsulation

&emsp Encapsulation is the property of a class to hide some of his data.
&emsp The role of encapsulation is to protect implementation details from the users.
&emsp In order to do that, attributes must be declared private and the setter and the getter methods must be public to modify and view the attributes values.

&emsp Example:
We have the Apple class.
With a private color attribute.
A constructor.
And a getter and setter method which will allowed user to modify and view the attributes values.

string.name: learn431
string.Data:
Final and Inheritance

Final

&emsp Final is a keyword which can be used in 2 ways:
1. With an attribute, which means that the attribute will not change his value.
2. With a class, which means that the class will not be inherited.

&emsp Example:
We have a final Fruit class which have a final /*color/* attribute.

string.name: learn432
string.Data:
Inheritance

&emsp Inheritance is the property of a class that enables one class to acquire the methods and attributes from another.
&emsp To inherit from a class we need to use the extends keyword.
&emsp The first class is name parent class or superclass and the class that inherit the first is named child class or subclass.
&emsp A class can extend only one class.

&emsp Example:
We have the Fruit superclass which have a color attribute, and a getColor method.
And we have the Apple subclass, which will inherit the color attribute and the getColor method.

resources.string: For what is used the \'final\' keyword on an attribute?

string.name: codelearn431
string.Data:
final class Fruit{
&emsp /* the Fruit class is final, which means the class can not be inherit anymore.*/

&emsp final String color= \"red\";
&emsp /* The attribute is final which means that is constant and its value can not be change anymore.*

string.name: codelearn432
string.Data:
class Fruit{
&emsp // Attributes:
&emsp String color= \"red\";
&emsp // get color method:
&emsp void getColor(){
&emsp &emsp return this.color;
&emsp }
&emsp // Constructors:
&emsp public Fruit(){}
}

&emspclass Apple extends Fruit {
&emsp // Attributes:
&emsp /*The \'color\' attribute already exist in the parent class(Fruit), so it will not be needed to be declared again.*/
&emsp // get color method:
&emsp /*The \'getColor\' method already exist in the parent class(Fruit), so it will not be needed to be implemented again.*/
&emsp // Constructors:
&emsp public Apple(){}


class Program{

&emsp public static void main(String[] args){

&emsp &emsp Fruit fruit = new Fruit();
&emsp &emsp Apples apple = new Apple();
&emsp &emsp System.out.println(fruit.getColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: red
&emsp &emsp System.out.println(apple.getColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: red

&emsp /*The \'getColor\' method of Apple class is the same with the method from Fruit class, because Apple class inherit all the attributes and the method from the parent class(Fruit class in this case).
So the output will be the value of the \'color\' attribute (red) which is declared in parent class*/
&emsp }
}

string.name: learn441
string.Data:
Polymorphism

&emsp Polymorphism is a property of the class similar to inheritance.
&emsp The difference between them is that the implementation of method can be rewritten in the subclass.

&emsp Example:
We have the Fruit parent class with a getColor method and two subclasses Apple and Banana with the getColor rewritten.

string.name: codelearn441
string.Data:
class Fruit{
&emsp // show color method:
&emsp void showColor(){
&emsp &emsp System.out.println(\"many colors\");
&emsp }
&emsp // Constructor:
&emsp public Fruit(){}
}

class Apple extends Fruit {
&emsp // show color method:
&emsp void showColor(){
&emsp &emsp System.out.println(\"green\");
&emsp }
&emsp // Constructor:
&emsp public Apple(){}
}

class Banana extends Fruit {
&emsp // show color method:
&emsp void showColor(){
&emsp &emsp System.out.println(\"yellow\");
&emsp }
&emsp // Constructor:
&emsp public Banana(){}
}


class Program{

&emsp public static void main(String[] args){

&emsp &emsp Fruit fruit = new Fruit();
&emsp &emsp Apples apple = new Apple();
&emsp &emsp Banana obj = new Banana();

&emsp &emsp fruit.showColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: many colors
&emsp &emsp apple.showColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: red
&emsp &emsp banana.showColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: yellow

&emsp &emsp /*The \'showColor\' method is rewritten for every subclass of Fruit class*/
&emsp }
}

string.name: learn451
string.Data:
Abstract class

&emsp An Abstract class is a class that contains abstract methods, but also regular methods and attributes.
&emsp An abstract method is a method that does not have any implementation and its role is to be inherit and modify by subclasses.

&emsp Example:
We have the \'Fruit\' abstract class with an abstract \'showColor\' method and a subclass \'Apple\' which will implement the showColor method.

its abstract methods will be implemented by a subclass
its methods can not be modify in a subclass
its abstract methods will be implemented by a subclass

abstract class Fruit{

&emsp }


class Program{

&emsp public static void main(String[] args){

&emsp &emsp Apples apple = new Apple();
&emsp &emsp apple.showColor());
&emsp &emsp // output: red

&emsp &emsp /*The abstract \'showColor\' method is implemented only in the \'Apple\' subclass.*/
&emsp }
}

string.name: learn461
string.Data:
Interface

&emsp An Interface is similar to the abstract class, but it has no regular attribute and no regular methods. It contains only non implemented methods.
&emsp A interface can be implemented using the word \'implements\'.
&emsp A class can implement as many interfaces as it needs.
&emsp A class can extends a superclass and implement other interfaces in the same time.

&emsp Example:
We have the \'IFruit\' interface with a non implemented \'showColor\' method and a class \'Apple\' which will implement the showColor method from the interface.

interface has only non implemented methods
interface has only non implemented methods

&emsp &emsp apple.showColor());
